title: Finite Q3 common-word OS Gram/KMS context Cauchy stress
question: For actual finite d=3 Q3 Hamiltonians on nested path volumes and registered shape controls, do identical local half-period OS words have a source-fixed, volume-Cauchy Gram/KMS envelope, or does finite context dependence remain visible?

model.common_word_test: Compare identical (source=0, beta, tau, observable) descriptors across nested path contexts
model.observables: A_x=exp(i a q_x/hbar), B_x=exp(i a p_x/hbar)

adversarial_review.check: Only the source-0 q/p character descriptors and the same beta/time grids are compared across contexts; no unproved tensor embedding is called an equality of Hamiltonians.
Every transfer factor uses exp(-s H/hbar), period beta*hbar, and the half-period reflection convention from EXP-001173.
The reported adjacent-context deltas are finite diagnostics only; a decreasing finite sequence is not promoted to a uniform thermodynamic Cauchy theorem.
Nested path contexts add the edge at the far boundary, but no locality estimate is assumed to make its effect vanish at the source.
Bond2, square4 and grid2x3 are separate finite controls and are never substituted for a path exhaustion.
The independent program reconstructs oscillator, tensor, Q3 Hamiltonian, spectral transfer, Gram, KMS and comparison values without importing the primary program.
Lean R247 checks exact finite Gibbs normalization/commutation and conditional transfer scope; dense Q3 spectral values and context deltas remain Python evidence.
Finite context comparisons cannot identify a common OS carrier, prove source/volume-uniform Cauchy control, establish one common alpha, a GNS gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.role: R247 supplies exact rational finite Gibbs checks and a scope firewall; Python supplies the dense finite Q3 context comparisons.

qft_interface.closed: For the declared finite contexts, the same source-0 transfer-word descriptors produce positive OS Gram matrices and finite KMS cyclicity, and their context deltas are explicitly computed.
qft_interface.open: The context deltas do not constitute a source/volume-uniform Cauchy estimate or an exhaustion-independent OS state. Common-word embedding, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common core, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum and physical TECT gates remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: If the finite deltas are bounded but nonzero, formulate an analytic source-to-boundary decay estimate with an explicit volume rate; if they fail to decrease or grow with context, register that as a route-local obstruction before attempting OS promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite d=3 context comparison. It is not a common OS carrier theorem, thermodynamic limit, common-alpha construction, mass-gap proof, continuum result, or QFT/Clay closure.
no_overclaim: This package proves only finite matrix transfer-word positivity, finite cyclicity, and explicit context-delta diagnostics for the declared graphs. It does not prove a thermodynamic OS measure, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, source/volume-uniform Cauchy convergence, a common alpha, a GNS mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
